## Motivation

An energy-based model assigns relative density through a scalar energy function.
Its [score]{.term key="score"} provides a local direction for a stochastic sampler, even when evaluating the [normalising constant]{.term key="normalising-constant"} is difficult.
The aim is to distinguish describing which outcomes are relatively likely from actually producing representative samples.

## Density and score {#energy-and-score}

Let $x\in\mathbb R^d$ be a possible observation and $E:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ a differentiable scalar energy function.
For a positive scale $\beta$, an energy model defines a density through the unnormalised weight $e^{-\beta E(x)}$:

$$
  \begin{aligned}
  p(x)&=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta E(x)},\\
  Z&=\int e^{-\beta E(x)}\,dx.
  \end{aligned}
$$

The same negative sign appears in the density and its normaliser.
Assume $Z$ is finite and $\beta>0$.
Then the score is $\nabla_x\ln p(x)=-\beta\nabla_xE(x)$, since $Z$ is constant with respect to $x$.
Energy is a scalar assigned to each candidate, while the score is a vector with one coordinate per input dimension.
The word energy here specifies a modelling function; a physical energy interpretation requires additional modelling assumptions.
Having an intractable normaliser is different from having no density specification at all.

## Score-based update {#langevin-dynamics}

Let $p$ be a differentiable target density and $\nabla_x\ln p(x)$ its score, as in an [energy-based model](energy-based-models.qmd).
Use a positive step size $\eta>0$.

One score-based Langevin discretisation is

$$
  x_{k+1}=x_k+\eta\nabla_x\ln p(x_k)
  +\sqrt{2\eta}\,\xi_k,
$$

with independent $\xi_k\sim\mathcal N(0,I)$.
The associated continuous diffusion has invariant density $p$ under suitable regularity and boundary conditions.
A finite-step discretisation generally has bias, and a finite run need not have mixed between modes.
Removing the noise gives [gradient ascent]{.term key="gradient-ascent"} on log density; it may approach a local mode and is not a general distribution sampler.
See [score-based generative modelling, Section 2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.13456) for the role of Langevin sampling.

## Example and boundaries

Take a scalar $x$ with energy $E(x)=x^2/2$ and $\beta=1$.
The normalised density is standard Gaussian, and its score is $-x$.
The Langevin update becomes $x_{k+1}=(1-\eta)x_k+\sqrt{2\eta}\,\xi_k$: drift pulls toward the centre while noise spreads the samples.
Without noise, $0<\eta<2$ makes repeated updates converge to zero, illustrating why locating the mode does not reproduce the Gaussian distribution.

A different limiting case is $E(x)=0$ on the whole real line.
Every point receives equal weight, but the integral is infinite, so these weights do not define a normalised probability density there.
Check integrability before interpreting an energy function as a probability model, and check discretisation error and mixing before interpreting a finite chain as target-distributed samples.
